name: North Watut
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Holzknecht, Susanne 1989. The Markham Languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115 (phonological sketches incl. Watut varieties); no open copy reachable.

sources.citation: Carter, John, John Grummitt, Janell Masters and Brian Paris. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of the Watut languages: South Watut [mcy], Middle Watut [mpl], and North Watut [una]. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-006. Dallas: SIL International. 87 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.5 (pp. 12-14) reproduces Holzknecht's consonant charts and explicitly declines to analyse phonology ('we therefore do not analyse our data in these areas'); Appendix C 170-item wordlists for the North Watut villages Onom, Uruf, Mafanazo carry no stress marks. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. doi 10.15144/PL-C115
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.8 North Watut (p. 55): phoneme table 4.9 plus four notes (voiced stop/prenasalised allophony, rare /k/, r~l, prothetic a); nothing on stress or accent. Ch. 4.1 says full phonological statements 'are to be published at a later date'. Only stress mentions in the book: folk perception of Adzera dialect differences (3.3), Duwet note 11 on unstressed vowel sequences, and a historical aside that the SWT/NWT final glottal replacing PMK *-n arose 'through stress rules' (4.6.23) -- no placement rule.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne C. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham and Ramu Valleys, PNG. PhD thesis, Australian National University. xxiii+446 pp. hdl 1885/133945
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Thesis version of the 1989 book; sec. 4.2.8 North Watut is word-for-word the same phoneme table and notes; full-text search finds the same three incidental stress mentions and no statement of stress placement for any Watut language.

sources.note: Markham family section 5.3.4 is historical phonology only; North Watut/Onank is not among the languages treated; no synchronic stress statement.
